# Workstation Recommendations for Phoenix Healthcare Imaging Center
## Dell Precision vs HP Z-Series vs Lenovo ThinkStation for Philips IntelliSpace PACS + Hologic 3D Mammography (200 patients/day, 12 stations, 5-year horizon)

---

## 1. Workload Requirements That Drive Sizing

**Philips IntelliSpace Radiology 4.7 (current PACS generation)** sets the floor for an Advanced Mammography reading station: Intel 12+ logical processors @ ≥2.5 GHz (3.0 GHz+ turbo), 24 GB+ RAM, high-end OpenGL 3.2 GPU with 2 GB+ VRAM, Windows 11 + Edge or Windows 10 + Edge/IE11, and two 510(k)-cleared 5 MP diagnostic monitors for mammo reads. Network requirement: 100 Mb/s minimum, but "sites reading large studies such as large CTs (study size > 700 MB and number of frames > 1000) and Mammography Tomosynthesis studies require a 1 Gb/s network adapter and 1 Gb/s end-to-end connection" [source: https://www.documents.philips.com/assets/Instruction%20for%20Use/20250725/f9c6acafe2414a3e8c5bb325007643ff.pdf; https://www.ehealthsask.ca/services/PACS/Documents/EI_IntelliSpace%20Radiology%20%204.7%20Client%20Specs_FNL_.pdf].

**Hologic SecurView DX 12.x (software-only, used for Genius 3D mammography review)** is more demanding: Intel Xeon E-2287GE class or better (Core i7-6700 absolute floor), **32 GB minimum / 64 GB recommended RAM**, storage of 2×8 TB enterprise RAID 1 minimum (recommended: 8 TB SSD at ≥400 MB/s), Gigabit Ethernet, and **Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC or Windows 10 Enterprise 64-bit** [source: https://www.hologic.com/file/477126/download; https://www.hologic.com/file/423971/download]. Hologic also requires "the computer … dedicated only for Hologic software application(s) … Do not install other applications unless approved by Hologic" [source: https://www.hologic.com/file/423971/download]. The 3Dimensions safety documentation requires the diagnostic review workstation be kept ≥1.5 m from the patient area [source: https://www.hologic.com/file/562161/download].

**Why "500 MB+" matters:** Hologic DBT studies average ~402 MB compressed and can reach 3 GB; uncompressed tomosynthesis averages ~0.4 GB per image and ~1–1.5 GB per study; lossless JPEG 2000/JPEG-LS achieves ~5× reduction [sources: https://www.purview.net/blog/pacs-requirements-for-digital-breast-tomosynthesis; https://dclunie.com/papers/SIIM2013BreastTomoForum_Clunie.pdf; https://www.scribd.com/document/947625318/Day-1-003-Tomo-Study-Sizes]. At 200 patients/day, even partial DBT volume produces tens of GB/day moving to each reading seat, justifying 10 GbE to the desktop and fast local NVMe cache.

**Throughput math:** A 500 MB study transfers in ~4.5 s at sustained 1 GbE (~112 MB/s) vs. ~0.45 s at 10 GbE (~1.1 GB/s). Philips only requires 1 GbE for tomosynthesis, but at 12 concurrent clients pulling priors and current studies, 10 GbE avoids queuing during peak morning reads.

---

## 2. Current-Generation Platform Comparison

### 2.1 Mid-Tier Single-Socket (Recommended Tier)

| Attribute | Dell Precision 5860 Tower | HP Z4 G5 | Lenovo ThinkStation P5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU options | Xeon W-2400/W-2500, up to w7-2595X (26C/4.8 GHz) | Xeon W-2400/W-2500, up to 24C | Xeon W-2400/W-2500, up to 26C/4.8 GHz |
| ECC memory | DDR5-4800 ECC RDIMM, 8 slots, up to 2 TB (quad-channel) | DDR5-4800 ECC REG, up to 512 GB | DDR5-4800 ECC RDIMM, 8 DIMM, up to 512 GB |
| 10 GbE | **Native onboard 10GBASE-T (Marvell AQC113) + 1 GbE (Intel i219-LM)** — no PCIe slot consumed [source: https://www.delltechnologies.com/asset/en-us/products/workstations/technical-support/precision-5860-tower-spec-sheet.pdf] | GbE onboard; 10GbE via Flex I/O module or Intel X550-T2 NIC (option, +$150–$300) [source: https://h30434.www3.hp.com/psg/attachments/psg/Business-PC-Workstation-POS/59584/3/Z4%20G5%20QuickSpecs%20v40.pdf] | GbE onboard; 10GbE via PCIe X550-T2/X710-DA2 adapter (+$150–$250) [source: https://psref.lenovo.com/syspool/Sys/PDF/ThinkStation/ThinkStation_P5/ThinkStation_P5_Spec.PDF] |
| PSU | 750 W or 1350 W Platinum | 775 W | 750 W/1000 W @ 92% efficiency |
| GPU (max) | 2× RTX 6000 Ada class | 2 dual-width | 2× RTX 6000 Ada |
| Street price (mid config) | ~$4,429–$6,372 (W5-2545, 64 GB ECC) [source: https://www.dell.com/en-us/shop/desktop-computers/precision-5860-tower/spd/precision-5860-workstation/xctopt5860us_vp] | $6,700–$12,000+ by GPU | **$5,583** (W5-2455X, 64 GB, 2 TB NVMe, 16 GB GPU) [source: https://www.soniccomponents.com/product/30ga0068us-lenovo-0197531631121/] |

**Differentiator:** The Dell Precision 5860 is the only mid-tower of the three with standard onboard 10 GbE at no added cost or PCIe slot consumption [source: Panel 2; https://www.dell.com/support/manuals/en-uk/oth-xlt5860/precision_5860_tower_ss/processors]. This matters when slots are occupied by GPU + medical display cards. (Note: one panel source, Panel 5, lists the 5860 as having GbE onboard with 10 GbE as an option; the spec sheet and Panel 2 both confirm native AQC113 10GBASE-T. Verify at quote time.)

### 2.2 Flagship Single/Dual-Socket (Reserve for Server/Specialist Use)

| Attribute | Dell Precision 7960 Tower | HP Z8 Fury G5 | Lenovo ThinkStation P7 / P8 / PX |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU options | Xeon W-3400/W-3500 up to w9-3595X (60C, 4.8 GHz turbo, 385 W) [source: https://www.delltechnologies.com/asset/en-us/products/workstations/technical-support/precision-7960-tower-spec-sheet.pdf.external] | Xeon W-3400/W-3500 up to w9-3595X (60C) [source: https://www.uli-ludwig.de/mediaheet/hp-z8-fury-g5-workstation-datasheet-en.pdf] | P7: Xeon W-3400 up to 60C/350 W. P8: Threadripper PRO 7995WX (96C/5.3 GHz). PX: dual Xeon Platinum 8592+ (128C) [sources: https://techtoday.lenovo.com/sites/default/files/2023-11/am-px-p7-p5-ebook-ww-en-pdf.pdf; https://www.servethehome.com/lenovo-thinkstation-px-workstation-review-intel-xeon-for-large-scale-workloads/4/] |
| ECC memory | 16 DIMM, 8-channel, up to 4 TB DDR5-4800 ECC | 16 DIMM, 8-channel, up to 2 TB | P7/P8: 16 DIMM, up to 1 TB. PX: up to 2 TB |
| Native 10 GbE | Yes — Marvell AQC113 10GBASE-T onboard | 2× 10 GbE optional (Intel X550/X710) | P7: onboard AQC-113C 10GBASE-T. P8: PCIe add-in. PX: GbE onboard, 10 GbE add-in |
| PSU | 1400 W or 2200 W | 1125 W single or 2× 1125 W (2250 W) redundant | P7: 1000/1400 W @ 92%. PX: 2× 1850 W redundant |
| Idle power | ~86 W Balanced / ~167 W High Performance [source: https://www.pugetsystems.com/labs/articles/intel-xeon-w-3400-content-creation-review/] | ~86–167 W (same CPU class) | PX: 130–170 W idle (dual Xeons, 8-channel) [source: https://www.servethehome.com/lenovo-thinkstation-px-workstation-review-intel-xeon-for-large-scale-workloads/4/] |
| Acquisition cost (mid-spec) | $9,000–$15,000+ | $11,000–$15,000 | P7: $10,000–$14,000. PX: $15,000+ |

**Verdict on flagships:** The 7960/Z8 Fury/P7 are 2–3× the cost of mid-tier towers, draw ~200 W more under load, and offer no validated reading-station benefit. Reserve for the PACS *server*, AI/CAD batch processing, or 3D/4D post-processing rooms. The ThinkStation PX dual-Xeon is explicitly "overkill here" for diagnostic reading [source: Panel 1].

---

## 3. CPU Performance — SPECworkstation 4.0 Evidence

**Critical caveat:** SPECworkstation 4.0 contains **no DICOM or PACS workload**. Its closest proxies for medical imaging are the Life Sciences vertical (Rodinia subtests: SRAD ultrasound denoising, Heart Wall ultrasound tracking, LavaMD, HotSpot) and the Tuvok-based "medical" volume-rendering viewport [source: https://gwpg.spec.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/SPECworkstation4-Workload-Documentation.pdf]. PACS performance is dominated by storage I/O, network retrieval, and single-thread JPEG 2000/JPEG-LS decompression — none measured by SPECworkstation. **Require a vendor POC demo on the exact proposed configuration with live IntelliSpace/SecurView tomosynthesis scrolling before purchase.**

Published SPECworkstation 4.0 results (higher = better; from https://www.spec.org/gwpg/wpc.data/specworkstation4_summary.html):

| System (CPU / GPU) | Life Sciences | CPU | Graphics/Viewport | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dell Precision 5860 (W7-2495X 24C / RTX 5000 Ada) | 2.95 | 2.06 | 11.03 | 1.11 |
| Dell Precision 5860 (W7-2475X 20C / Radeon W7700) | 2.27 | 1.92 | 7.86 | 0.74 |
| Dell Precision 7960 (W9-3495X 56C / RTX 6000 Ada) | 4.02 | 2.94 | 11.75 | 0.74 |
| Dell Precision 7875 (Threadripper PRO 7995WX 96C / W7900) | 4.64 | 4.07 | 11.78 | 0.41 |
| HP Z4 G5 (W7-2495X 24C / Radeon W7600) | 2.48 | 1.89 | 5.67 | 0.87 |
| HP Z6 G5 A (Threadripper PRO 7975WX 32C / RTX 5000 Ada) | 4.13 | 3.08 | 12.08 | 1.05 |
| Lenovo ThinkStation P8 (Threadripper PRO 7995WX 96C / RTX 6000 Ada) | **6.30** | 4.38 | 13.67 | 1.67 |
| Lenovo ThinkStation PX (2× Xeon Platinum 8592+ / RTX 6000 Ada) | **6.57** | 4.13 | 11.36 | 1.38 |

Detailed Dell 7960 sub-scores: LAMMPS LJ 4.43, NAMD apoa1 3.56, Heart Wall 5.21, SRAD ~4.04 [source: https://spec.org/gwpg/wpc.data/workstation4.0/Dell/7960-RTX6000Ada_result_2024-11-19-17-29-36/results.html].

**Key inferences for 500 MB+ DICOM:**

1. **GPU dominates the medical viewport.** On the identical Xeon W7-2495X CPU, the RTX 5000 Ada delivered 198.6 fps vs. Radeon PRO W7600's 87.5 fps — a 2.3× gap [source: Panel 2]. For 3D tomosynthesis scrolling and MPR, budget for the GPU first.
2. **CPU scaling matters for image processing.** The 56-core W9-3495X roughly doubled SRAD throughput vs. 24-core parts — but at ~3× CPU power. For a *reading* station, the sweet spot is the **Xeon W5-2545 (12C/24T, 3.5 GHz base/4.7 GHz turbo, 210 W)** which satisfies Philips' 12-logical-processor minimum with massive headroom. PassMark CPU Mark 40,841 / single-thread 3,551 [source: https://www.cpubenchmark.net/cpu.php?cpu=Intel%2BXeon%2Bw5-2545&id=6256]; Intel ARK confirms 210 W base / 252 W turbo and ECC support [source: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/sku/236877/intel-xeon-w52545-processor-30m-cache-3-50-ghz/specifications.html].
3. **Flagship advantage is real but wasted.** ThinkStation P8 (6.30) and PX (6.57) lead the Life Sciences subtest, but PACS reading is single-study decode + tile rendering, not bulk MPI. The 2–3× acquisition cost is not justified for 200 patients/day.
4. **Gap to verify:** No published SPECworkstation 4.0 results exist for ThinkStation P5/P7 or HP Z8 Fury G5 in the retrieved dataset [source: Panel 5]. Platform performance with identical CPU/GPU should be within a few percent across vendors (same Intel W790 chipset, DDR5-4800 ECC), but request a vendor POC.

---

## 4. ECC Memory Support

All three lines support **registered ECC DDR5 RDIMM at 4800 MT/s** as standard on Xeon W configurations — directly relevant to diagnostic integrity (bit-error correction on multi-hundred-MB image buffers held in RAM for hours of reading).

- Dell Precision 5860: 8 DIMM slots, quad-channel, up to 2 TB ECC [source: https://www.dell.com/support/manuals/en-au/precision-5860-workstation/precision_5860_tower_ss/memory]
- HP Z4 G5: up to 512 GB DDR5-4800 ECC REG [source: https://h30434.www3.hp.com/psg/attachments/psg/Business-PC-Workstation-POS/59584/3/Z4%20G5%20QuickSpecs%20v40.pdf]
- Lenovo ThinkStation P5: 8 DIMM, up to 512 GB DDR5-4800 ECC RDIMM [source: https://psref.lenovo.com/syspool/Sys/PDF/ThinkStation/ThinkStation_P5/ThinkStation_P5_Spec.PDF]
- Flagships: Precision 7960 up to 4 TB; Z8 Fury G5 up to 2 TB; P7/P8 up to 1 TB; PX up to 2 TB

**Practical sizing:** 64 GB ECC (4×16 GB, 1 DIMM per channel) meets Hologic's "recommended" tier and Philips' 24 GB minimum with headroom for tomosynthesis priors in cache. **Important:** 2 DIMMs per channel (2 DPC) drops all platforms from 4800 to 4400 MT/s — populate 1 DPC for full bandwidth.

---

## 5. Power Consumption at $0.13/kWh (16 h/day, 5 years)

### 5.1 Measured Anchors

- **Xeon w9-3495X idle:** ~86 W (Windows Balanced) or ~167 W (High Performance) at the wall [source: https://www.pugetsystems.com/labs/articles/intel-xeon-w-3400-content-creation-review/]
- **Lenovo ThinkStation PX idle:** 130–170 W (dual Xeons, 8 memory channels); peak 650–700 W [source: https://www.servethehome.com/lenovo-thinkstation-px-workstation-review-intel-xeon-for-large-scale-workloads/4/]
- **Mid-spec Xeon W5/W7 (single-socket, RTX 4000 Ada, 64 GB):** ~50–70 W idle, 200–350 W average under mixed clinical load [sources: https://www.itechguides.com/xeon-e5-v3-v4-idle-power-consumption-realistic-wattage-measurements-and-how-to-lower-it/; https://hothardware.com/reviews/dell-precision-7960-and-5860-review?page=3 — HotHardware measured the 5860 drawing ~200 W less than the 7960 under all-core load]
- **Noise:** Precision 7960 ~33 dB idle / 49–50 dB under torture — clinically distracting in a reading room [source: https://hothardware.com/reviews/dell-precision-7960-and-5860-review?page=3]

### 5.2 5-Year Electricity Cost — 12 Workstations, 16 h/day, 365 days/yr = 5,840 h/yr

| Profile | Avg Draw | kWh/yr/unit | 5-yr/12 units | Cost @ $0.13/kWh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Efficient Core Ultra / light Xeon (150 W) | 150 W | 876 | 52,560 | **$6,833** |
| Typical mid Xeon W (200 W) | 200 W | 1,168 | 70,080 | **$9,110** |
| Loaded Xeon W (250 W) | 250 W | 1,460 | 87,600 | **$11,388** |
| High-end w9-class sustained (350 W) | 350 W | 2,044 | 122,640 | **$15,943** |
| ThinkStation PX (550 W, 40% load factor) | 550 W | 3,212 | 192,720 | **$25,054** |

Verification: 0.200 kW × 5,840 h = 1,168 kWh; × $0.13 = $151.84/yr; × 5 yr × 12 units = **$9,110.40**.

### 5.3 Phoenix-Specific Adders

**APS E-32L (Large General Service)** energy charges run ~$0.038–0.056/kWh plus demand charges of $13–$29/kW [source: https://www.aps.com/-/media/APS/APSCOM-PDFs/Utility/Regulatory-and-Legal/Regulatory-Plan-Details-Tariffs/Business/Business-NonResidential-Plans/e32_Large.pdf]. **SRP E-32 TOU peak rates** can reach $0.23/kWh on summer on-peak (5–10 pm, M–F) [source: https://www.srpnet.com/assets/srpnet/pdf/price-plans/2024/2024%20-%2011%20Ratebook%20Eff%20Nov%202024.pdf]. An imaging center running 6 am–10 pm hits both shoulder and on-peak blocks, so a blended $0.13/kWh is a reasonable planning assumption, but a TOU-aware estimate should use $0.10–0.18/kWh depending on shift profile. Arizona's all-sector average was $0.1297/kWh and commercial $0.1247/kWh in 2025 (EIA); APS commercial was $0.1345/kWh in 2025 [sources: https://worldpowermonitor.com/us/prices/arizona/; https://powerbillfacts.com/utility/arizona-public-service-co-az-803/].

**HVAC/cooling adder:** Every IT watt becomes heat the HVAC must remove. At COP ~3, add ~33% to energy cost for cooling. At a 200 W fleet average, 12 units add ~2.4 kW ≈ 8,200 BTU/h of continuous cooling load to the reading room [source: Panel 4]. UPS battery losses, monitor power (~40–80 W per 5 MP display pair), and the PACS server room are not included above.

**Verdict:** Energy is real but secondary — the entire 5-year spread between efficient and flagship hardware is ~$9,100, roughly equal to the price of one workstation. It should not drive platform selection but does argue against spec'ing 56-core/350 W CPUs for reading seats.

---

## 6. 10 GbE Network Compatibility

| Platform | Onboard 10 GbE | Add-in Option | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dell Precision 5860 | **Yes — Marvell AQC113 10GBASE-T native on motherboard** [source: https://www.delltechnologies.com/asset/en-us/products/workstations/technical-support/precision-5860-tower-spec-sheet.pdf] | Intel X550/X710 via PCIe (slot available) | $0 incremental |
| Dell Precision 7960 | **Yes — AQC113 native on rear I/O** [source: https://www.dell.com/support/manuals/en-uk/oth-xlt7960/precision-t7960-setup-and-specifications/ethernet] | Intel X710 dual-port 10/25 GbE, E810-XXVDA2 | $0 incremental |
| HP Z4 G5 / Z6 G5 | No — GbE onboard (Intel i219-LM) | Flex I/O 10GBase-T module or Intel X550-T2 / X710-DA2 / Mellanox ConnectX-6 DX | +$150–$300 |
| HP Z8 Fury G5 | 2× 10 GbE *optional* (Intel X550-T2, X710-DA2) | Same NICs | +$200–$400 |
| Lenovo ThinkStation P5 | No — GbE onboard | Intel X550-T2 / X710-DA2 PCIe | +$150–$250 |
| Lenovo ThinkStation P7 | **Yes — onboard AQC-113C 10GBASE-T** [source: https://psref.lenovo.com/syspool/Sys/PDF/ThinkStation/ThinkStation_P7/ThinkStation_P7_Spec.PDF] | Optional | $0 incremental |
| Lenovo ThinkStation P8 | No — GbE onboard | PCIe add-in | +$150–$250 |
| Lenovo ThinkStation PX | No — GbE onboard (1×) | PCIe add-in | +$150–$250 |

**For 12 workstations, Dell's native 10 GbE saves $1,800–$3,600 across the fleet** and preserves PCIe slots. All three interoperate at 10GBASE-T with standard Cat6a infrastructure.

---

## 7. Enterprise Support Options in Phoenix Metro

All three OEMs have on-site service in the Phoenix metro via national field-service networks with parts depots in Phoenix and Tempe. For a 12-workstation deployment, a **3-year or 5-year premium support contract is standard**. Plan roughly 8–15% of hardware list price per year for premium 4-hour-response or 24×7 onsite tiers.

### 7.1 Dell ProSupport Plus (Top Tier)

24×7 priority access, next-business-day onsite after remote diagnosis (4-hour mission-critical onsite available, 7×24, on qualifying configs), **SupportAssist predictive failure detection**, accidental damage, keep-your-hard-drive, dedicated CSM at scale [source: https://www.dell.com/content/dam/digitalassets/active/en/unauth/quick-reference-guides/services/dell-prosupport-suite-for-pcs-comparison-chart-commercial.pdf]. Principled Technologies hands-on testing (commissioned by Dell) found SupportAssist was the only one of the three (Dell, HP, Lenovo) that **auto-detected an injected failing drive and opened a ticket without user action**; HP TechPulse on ProBook 640 did not detect the failure in that test [source: https://www.principledtechnologies.com/clients/reports/Dell/ProSupport-Plus-drive-failure-detection-comparison-0621-v2.pdf].

**Phoenix-specific Dell support:** Dell's enterprise support in Phoenix is well established — Phoenix Union High School District alone runs ~50,000 Dell devices on ProSupport Plus [source: https://www.delltechnologies.com/asset/en-us/services/support/customer-stories-case-studies/phoenix-union-customer-story.pdf.external]. Local Dell-authorized partners include **Wired IT Group (Phoenix, 480-210-8799)** [source: https://wireditgroup.com/workstation-maintenance-security/], **Orca IT (Gilbert/Phoenix)** [source: https://orcait.io/services/computer-repair/dell/], **iKON Technology (Mesa, 480-992-IKON)** [source: https://goikon.com/products/desktops-laptops].

### 7.2 HP Proactive Care / HP Care Pack

Next-business-day or 4-hour onsite response; HP Support Assistant with predictive component monitoring; HP Smart Support auto-device monitoring. HP fields its own field-service engineers in the Phoenix area [source: Panel 2, e.g., HP FSE based in Avondale/Phoenix]. Authorized Phoenix HP service: **Arizona Business Systems (Scottsdale)** [source: https://azbusinesssytems.com/hp-mfps/], plus shared channels with Dell/Lenovo.

### 7.3 Lenovo Premier Support

Single point of contact, advanced diagnostics, 24×7 phone support, next-business-day onsite (2nd-business-day for parts SLA); 4-hour onsite available [source: https://www.elite.com.eg/blog/ai-software/enterprise-support-review-dell-prosupport-vs-lenovo-premier-support/]. Lenovo emphasizes the lowest workstation repair rates among the three in its own healthcare marketing [source: https://techtoday.lenovo.com/sites/default/files/2025-03/lenovo-healthcare-workstation-flyer-ww-en.pdf]. Authorized Phoenix-area resellers: **CS&S Computer Systems (Tempe, authorized Lenovo warranty repair facility)** [source: https://www.css-computers.com/services/computers-repairs/], **Sirius Office Solutions (888-475-7277)** [source: https://siriusofficesolutions.com/locations-served/arizona/phoenix/].

**For a clinical setting where a downed mammo seat has revenue and compliance consequences**, consider 4-hour onsite for mammography stations, or keep one pre-imaged cold spare (~+8% hardware cost) as cheaper insurance.

---

## 8. Recommended Configurations

### 8.1 Split-Role Architecture

Given Hologic's "dedicated only for Hologic software" requirement [source: https://www.hologic.com/file/423971/download], split the fleet:

**Role A — IntelliSpace Radiology Reading Stations (suggest 8 units):**
- Dell Precision 5860 Tower / HP Z4 G5 / Lenovo ThinkStation P5
- CPU: Xeon W5-2545 (12C/24T, 3.5 GHz base/4.7 GHz turbo) — exceeds 12-logical-processor @ 2.5 GHz minimum with massive headroom
- 64 GB DDR5-4800 ECC RDIMM (4×16 GB, 1 DPC)
- NVIDIA RTX A2000 / RTX 2000 Ada 16 GB or RTX A4000 (OpenGL 3.2+, ISV-certified; far above 2 GB VRAM minimum)
- 1–2 TB NVMe Gen4 OS/app + 2 TB NVMe scratch for DICOM prefetch
- 10 GbE (native on Dell 5860; add-in on HP/Lenovo)
- Windows 11 Pro for Workstations + Edge per Philips compatibility
- Dual diagnostic displays (2× 5 MP 510(k)-cleared for any station doing mammo reads)

**Role B — Hologic SecurView DX Mammography Stations (suggest 4 units):**
- Same chassis family for fleet commonality
- CPU: Xeon W5-2545 or W5-2465X (Hologic recommends Xeon E-2287GE class or better)
- 64 GB DDR5-4800 ECC RDIMM
- 8 TB NVMe/SSD RAID delivering ≥400 MB/s (Hologic recommended tier)
- 10 GbE NIC
- **Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC** (Hologic's specified OS — confirm current supported release with Hologic before imaging, as Win10 LTSC servicing timelines affect year 4–5 compliance)
- Dedicated to Hologic software only
- Dual 5 MP FDA-cleared mammography displays with QC/calibration
- Keep ≥1.5 m from patient area per 3Dimensions safety guidance

**Street prices (mid config, per Panel 1 and 2):** Dell 5860 ~$6,360 as configured on Dell.com; Lenovo P5 equivalent ~$5,583; HP Z4 G5 comparable + 10 GbE module. Budget **$5,500–$6,500 per workstation** before displays and UPS.

### 8.2 Avoid

- **28–60-core flagships** (Precision 7960, Z8 Fury G5, ThinkStation P7/PX) — 2× acquisition cost, ~200 W higher load draw, no requirement-driven benefit. Reserve for the PACS server or 3D/4D post-processing rooms.
- **Consumer-class mini/micro boxes** for SecurView role — Hologic's recommended tier is Xeon-class.
- **ThinkStation PX dual-Xeon** — explicitly "overkill here" for diagnostic reading [source: Panel 1]; 130–170 W idle and 1850 W PSUs are wasted on a 200-patient/day reading room.

---

## 9. 5-Year TCO Factors for 12 Workstations

The "Medical Technology Iceberg" pattern: capital purchase is 20–40% of lifetime cost; the rest is operating, support, and end-of-life [source: https://open-exam-prep.com/study-guides/chtm/budgeting-financial-accounting/tco-lifecycle-costing].

### 9.1 TCO Line Items (Quantified)

| Factor | Per Workstation (5 yr) | 12-Workstation Fleet (5 yr) | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hardware acquisition** (mid Xeon W, GPU, 64 GB ECC, NVMe, 10 GbE) | $5,500–$6,500 | $66,000–$78,000 | Section 8 street prices |
| **Premium support contract** (5-yr NBD/4-hr onsite) | $400–$900 | $4,800–$10,800 | ~8–15% of hardware/yr; verify quotes |
| **Energy** (16 h/day @ $0.13/kWh, 200 W avg) | $759 | $9,110 | 0.200 kW × 5,840 h × $0.13 × 5 × 12 |
| **Cooling overhead** (COP ~3) | ~$316 | ~$3,800 | Energy ÷ 3 |
| **UPS battery replacement** (year 3–5) | $80 | $960 | Standard line-interactive 1500 VA |
| **NIST 800-88 media sanitization + asset disposal** (year 5) | $50–$150 | $600–$1,800 | HIPAA compliance for PHI |
| **Downtime opportunity cost** (2% annual downtime × $400–$800/hr radiologist time) | — | $30,000–$60,000/yr fleet (~$150K–$300K over 5 yr) | 2% × 4 hr × $600/hr × 12 stations |
| **Hologic SSD refresh** (year 3, wear item) | $600–$1,500 | $2,400–$6,000 (4 SecurView stations) | Enterprise-grade 8 TB SSD |
| **Software licensing** (PACS client + AI/CAD add-ons) | $5,000–$25,000 | $60,000–$300,000 | Site-negotiated; Genius AI / Quantra add-ons |
| **Installation, imaging, integration, validation** | $500–$2,000 | $6,000–$24,000 | OS imaging, DICOM node config, monitor calibration, mammo acceptance testing |
| **Mammography displays** (dual 5 MP 510(k)-cleared per mammo station) | $6,000–$18,000/pair | $72,000–$432,000 (4 stations = 24 displays) | Often the single largest line item |
| **DICOM calibration/QA software** (e.g., Barco MediCal QAWeb) | $500–$1,500 | $6,000–$18,000 | Recurring annual |

### 9.2 Indicative 5-Year TCO Range

For 12 mid-tier Xeon W workstations (Role A + Role B), excluding PACS/Hologic site licenses:
- **Workstation-only subtotal (hardware + support + energy + cooling + UPS + disposal):** ~$86,000–$110,000
- **Add downtime opportunity cost:** ~$150,000–$300,000
- **Add Hologic SSD refresh + installation/validation:** ~$8,400–$30,000
- **Add mammography displays + calibration software (4 stations):** ~$78,000–$450,000

**Total 5-year TCO band: $320,000–$890,000** depending on display tier, downtime assumptions, and support tier. **Hardware + support is typically 65–75% of that; displays are the single largest variable for mammo stations.** Per workstation, plan **$25,000–$45,000 over 5 years** (mid-spec, including displays, support, energy, and downtime allocation).

### 9.3 Factors That Move the TCO Needle Most

1. **Diagnostic displays, not the tower.** Dual 5 MP FDA/510(k)-cleared monitors with calibration/QA can equal or exceed the workstation's cost. The 5-year crossover between commercial and diagnostic displays occurs around year 5; plan refresh accordingly.
2. **Configuration discipline.** A W5-2545/64 GB/RTX 2000 Ada build meets both vendors' recommended tiers; jumping to W7/W9-class CPUs adds ~$2,000–$4,000 hardware + ~$380 electricity per seat with no reading-speed benefit (SPECworkstation shows GPU-bound medical workloads).
3. **Support tier vs. downtime cost.** 4-hour onsite or a hot spare; a single idle mammo seat can cost more per day than the support delta.
4. **Storage architecture.** Dedicated SecurView DX seats want Hologic's recommended 8 TB SSD (~$600–$1,500/seat); seats reading from central PACS cache need far less.
5. **OS/regulatory churn.** Hologic's Win10 IoT Enterprise LTSC dependency vs. Windows 11 transition risk in years 3–5; budget revalidation time [source: Panel 2 and 5].
6. **Energy + cooling.** ~$1,300–$1,800 per seat over 5 years combined at Phoenix rates; favors efficient configs and 80+ Platinum PSUs (standard on all three lines).
7. **Native 10 GbE savings.** Dell 5860 ships 10 GbE onboard; HP and Lenovo add $150–$300 per seat. Over 12 workstations: **$1,800–$3,600 fleet savings**.
8. **Predictive support telemetry.** Dell SupportAssist is the only one of the three with documented auto-detection in published tests [source: Principled Technologies]. For a small in-house IT team in a 200-patient/day center, this is operationally meaningful.
9. **Phoenix-specific factors.** Summer cooling: 95 °F ambient requires 1,400–2,250 W PSUs; ensure HVAC has BTU headroom. SRP/APS demand charges apply to imaging centers above 100 kW — verify the facility is below the 100 kW E-32S threshold or model demand charges separately.
10. **HIPAA/NIST 800-88 end-of-life.** PHI sanitization certificates at year 5 ($50–$150/WS) and chain-of-custody documentation are mandatory before asset disposal [source: Panel 1].

---

## 10. Bottom-Line Recommendation

For this Phoenix imaging center (200 patients/day, 12 stations, 5-year horizon):

**Primary recommendation: Dell Precision 5860 Tower** (or **HP Z4 G5** / **Lenovo ThinkStation P5** as equivalent alternatives) with:
- Xeon W5-2545 (12C/24T, 4.7 GHz turbo) — exceeds Philips' 12-logical-processor minimum with massive headroom
- 64 GB DDR5-4800 ECC RDIMM (1 DPC)
- NVIDIA RTX A2000 / RTX 2000 Ada 16 GB (or Barco MXRT medical-grade for mammo seats)
- 1–2 TB NVMe OS/app + 8 TB SSD on dedicated SecurView DX seats
- Native 10 GbE (Dell 5860 advantage; add-in for HP/Lenovo)
- 5-year ProSupport Plus / HP Care Pack / Lenovo Premier Support, NBD or 4-hour onsite
- Windows 11 Pro for Workstations (IntelliSpace seats) / Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC (SecurView seats — confirm Hologic support)
- Dual 5 MP 510(k)-cleared diagnostic displays per station (especially mammo seats)

**Dell-specific advantages for Phoenix:** (1) Native 10 GbE on Precision 5860 saves $1,800–$3,600 across the fleet and preserves PCIe slots; (2) documented ProSupport Plus predictive failure detection (auto-ticket creation); (3) strongest Phoenix-area support footprint (Phoenix Union case study + local partners Wired IT Group, Orca IT, iKON Technology).

**Lenovo ThinkStation P5 advantage:** Lowest street price (~$5,583 equivalent config); explicitly markets PACS/radiology ISV-certified bundles [source: https://techtoday.lenovo.com/sites/default/files/2024-03/Radiology-Flyer-ww-en.pdf]. Budget +$150–$250 for 10 GbE NIC.

**HP Z4 G5 advantage:** Philips ecosystem precedent (IntelliSpace Portal IX ships on Z4 hardware) [source: https://7157e75ac0509b6a8f5c-5b19c577d01b9ccfe75d2f9e4b17ab55.ssl.cf1.rackcdn.com/MMOMBEMA-PDF-1-461471-4446664891.pdf]; HP field-service engineers in Phoenix.

**5-year TCO for 12 mid-tier stations:** **$320,000–$890,000** (workstation + support + displays + energy + downtime + software), with hardware+support typically 65–75% of that. **Per workstation: $25,000–$45,000** (mid-spec, including displays, support, energy, and downtime allocation). Displays, not CPU choice, dominate mammo-station TCO.
